questions.question_text:
A motif slides $5$ squares left and $3$ squares up without turning.
Which description is complete?

options.why: Reverses the horizontal and vertical distances in the stated slide.
Uses both opposite directions, describing the inverse translation.
Keeps the horizontal direction but reverses the vertical direction.

questions.solution_text:
The movement is already a slide, so record its horizontal and vertical parts in their stated directions.
Translation $5$ squares left and $3$ squares up

questions.question_text:
An arrow pointing east turns to point north about $O$.
What is the smallest rotation?

options.why: Turns east towards south, using the opposite direction around the centre.
Uses a half-turn, which would make the east-pointing arrow point west.
Takes the long anticlockwise turn, which is equivalent to 90 degrees clockwise.

questions.solution_text:
A quarter-turn anticlockwise takes east to north.
Rotation $90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise about $O$

Counts four squares right but reverses the downward vertical direction.

questions.solution_text:
$M$ moves from $(0.5,3.4)$ to $(4.5,0.4)$: $4$ squares right and $3$ squares down.
Translation $4$ squares right and $3$ squares down

questions.question_text:
The same-size shapes are on opposite sides of a dashed line.
Which extra fact proves the transformation is a reflection?

options.text: They are mirror images equally far from the line

options.why: Uses a fact shared by translation, reflection and rotation, so it does not identify reflection.
Describes a translation-like orientation instead of a mirror reversal.

options.text: They are the same distance from a point
options.why: Uses a rotation clue involving a centre rather than a mirror-line condition.

questions.solution_text:
A reflection flips the shape and places matching points the same perpendicular distance from the mirror line.
They are mirror images equally far from the line.

questions.question_text:
A marker points south-east, then points north-west after turning about $K$.
What is the smallest rotation?

options.why: Uses a quarter-turn, which takes south-east to south-west rather than north-west.
Uses a quarter-turn, which takes south-east to north-east rather than north-west.
Uses a full turn, which returns the marker to south-east instead of reversing it.

questions.solution_text:
South-east and north-west are opposite directions, so the marker makes a half-turn.
Rotation $180^{\circ}$ about $K$
